page.layout: One page of text in a single column of verses, numbered 17 to 24 in the left margin, each verse a two- or four-line stanza. Below the last verse, at the lower right, the catchword "ARGV-". Running head at top. A strip of the neighbouring page is visible at the right edge and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: 17 Scandala fac caveas, fratrique remittere sæpe Convenit: haud factis est tribuenda salus. Bis quinque à lepra mundantur, at unus eidem est gratus: quàm sit dura suprema dies,
18 Sæpius orandum est: duo sunt, qui limina templi Intrant: & pueros dextera sancta tegit. Dimittibus gravis est via vitæ, præmia sanctis Magna jacent: sano lumine cæcus abit.
19 Excipit unigenam dives Zachæus Jesum, Distribuit servis multa talenta suis. Conscendens asinam Solymarum tristia fata Flet: sancta merces ejicit atque domo.
20 Quislicita, inquirunt, dederit sibi iura docendi, Agricolæ domino debita vina negant. Reddatis censum: defuncti à morte resurgunt. CHRISTUS Davidi sit filius & Dominus.
21 Parvula laudantur vidua munuscula grata, Excidium templi duraque fata canit. Sint vigiles animi: fortis patientia servat. Hæc etenim grandis pœna futura brevi[?] est.

22 Doctorem turpi precio[?] divendit Judas, Instituit cœnam, corda superba notat. Sit gladius vobis: offerte sua vota parentis: Dum capitur fortis dimicat ense Petrus. Sed negat infelix hunc quem defenderat ante, Illusus CHRISTUS verbera multa tulit.

23 Pontius Herodi CHRISTUM transmittit iniqua Barrabam immanem vult tenuisse cohors. Sistitur ploratus: ligno dependet ab alto. Latroni sæno[?] gratia læta datur. Multa necem pariter testantur signa nefandam: Et nova defuncti marmora corpus habent.

24 Angelus hic Mariæ enarrat vivere CHRISTUM, Cumque alias vivens urbem Emaunta petit. Apparens rursum, sumto se vivere pisce Approbat & toto in orbe docere jubet. Scripturam enarrans cœlum conscendit in altum, Ad Solymas redit cum pia turba domus.

page.notes: A short dash stands in the margin beside verse 24; no text. Doubtful readings: "Doctorem" (first word of verse 22, the letters are hard to separate), "precio" (possibly "pretio"), "brevi" (the last letters are unclear), "sæno" (possibly "fæno"), "offerte" (possibly "offert"). Verse 20 "Quislicita" and "Reddatis" are copied as printed. The image is cut off on the left by a glass or lens glare, which is not printed text.
